title: Biodegradation Testing of Difficult Substances in Surface Water
author: Birch, Hammershøj, et al.

steps.title: Collect and transport surface water
steps.instruction: Sample surface water as quickly as possible, transport to the laboratory promptly, and if transport exceeds 2–3 hours cool the sample to 4 °C; otherwise keep the water at sampling or test temperature and store for less than one day before use.

steps.title: Characterize and report inoculum properties
steps.instruction: Record the geographic origin and type of the surface‑water inoculum and measure total suspended solids, dissolved organic carbon, relevant nutrients (for seawater), and selected microbial parameters such as heterotrophic plate count.

steps.title: Prepare closed, inert test vials
steps.instruction: Use gas‑tight 20 mL headspace vials compatible with an autosampler; construct the system from glass and PTFE only (no plastic contact with water or headspace) and keep the vials sealed and un‑aerated throughout incubation, never opening them before extraction/analysis.

steps.title: Add inoculum to vials
steps.instruction: Transfer 15 mL of the collected surface‑water inoculum into each 20 mL vial, leaving a 5 mL headspace; adjust the headspace if a higher initial oxygen level is required. When using passive dosing, the spike solution may constitute up to 10 % of the vial volume, and the water volume should be reduced accordingly.

steps.title: Prepare abiotic control vials
steps.instruction: Prepare control vials exactly as the biotic ones but substitute the inoculum with pure water; if the original inoculum contains low suspended solids and low dissolved organic matter, pure water is sufficient. For high dissolved organic matter, filter‑sterilize the water; if particles are abundant and sorption is expected, use autoclaved or chemically poisoned controls as described in OECD 309.

steps.title: Spike test chemicals into vials
steps.instruction: Using gas‑tight syringes (passive dosing) or automated micro‑volume syringes, dispense the test chemical(s) below the water surface in each vial, then close the vial immediately to prevent loss of volatile compounds.

steps.title: Incubate test systems and sample
steps.instruction: Incubate the sealed vials under the chosen temperature conditions; at each predetermined measurement time remove the required number of biotic and abiotic vials and transfer them directly to the autosampler for analysis. Measurement intervals are chemical‑ and water‑specific and cannot be universally fixed.

steps.title: Handle autosampler storage to prevent degradation
steps.instruction: If no sample‑conservation step is used, do not leave vials on the autosampler for extended periods; when incubation is at low temperature and the autosampler is not temperature‑controlled, minimize the time vials remain on the autosampler because temperature changes accelerate degradation.

steps.title: Analyze samples by SPME‑GC‑MS
steps.instruction: Perform Solid Phase Microextraction (SPME) coupled to GC‑MS; choose headspace SPME for volatile chemicals or immersion SPME for less volatile, hydrophobic chemicals, and optimise the fiber and column for the specific analytes. Alternate analysis of biotic and abiotic samples to correct for signal drift, clean the SPME fiber between runs to reduce carry‑over, and recognise that degradation below the analytical carry‑over limit will not be detected.
